risks.title: API observation/IP trust
risks.scenario: Network exposure with observe or shared proxy identity.
risks.controls: Enforce rejects unknown clients; credential identities available. Since router 0.22.1 the posture report (router.py --posture, start log; ADR-0064) states observe mode, an unlocked policy, shared tokens, address-only clients, a control port without login and an API port without TLS. Since router 0.23.0 (ADR-0067) router.py --init writes a first configuration without placeholder secrets, and the posture report flags a well-known example token and a control port on the network without TLS.
risks.next_action: Run the posture report before every rollout and resolve or accept each finding; proxy/IP behaviour in the deployment.
risks.validation_gap: V1: proxy/IP behavior needs deployment tests.

risks.title: Control behind a local proxy
risks.scenario: Proxy enters the unauthenticated loopback exception.
risks.controls: A control port without users answers 503, also on loopback (ADR-0053); unauthenticated loopback only with the boolean control_auth.allow_unauthenticated_loopback, a literal loopback listener and a loopback peer; a start warning names the state.
risks.next_action: Keep the regression in CI; deployments behind a proxy configure Control users and TLS.
risks.validation_gap: V2: a real reverse-proxy topology is not part of CI; the unit tests model its loopback peer.
risks.evidence: selftest_security: loopback peer without users is refused (503, handler not called) unless the switch is set; the switch does not open remote peers or a wildcard listener; the check fails against router 0.18.2.

risks.title: Admin browser attacks
risks.scenario: Cross-site admin request or same-origin compromise.
risks.controls: Non-simple header and Fetch Metadata checks. Since router 0.22.2 (ADR-0065) inline-handler values go through js() (JSON string literal, HTML-escaped), esc() escapes the single quote, the control port sends a CSP (connect-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none', no foreign code) and X-Frame-Options DENY, both ports nosniff and no referrer, and no CORS header.
risks.next_action: Move inline handlers to addEventListener and drop 'unsafe-inline'; segment admin access.
risks.validation_gap: V3: headers, CORS and handler escaping are tested in CI and were checked once in a real browser; inline markup injection under 'unsafe-inline' is not excluded.

risks.title: Concrete-model authorization
risks.scenario: Role-limited client chooses a concrete model.
risks.controls: Concrete model names need an explicit boolean models:true (ADR-0052); a missing setting means roles only and is named in a load-time warning; a non-boolean value is a configuration error.
risks.next_action: Consider per-client model allowlists; keep the grant tests in CI.
risks.validation_gap: Model listings still show concrete names to role-only clients (information, not access). Both proxy call sites use auth.client_allows; protocol coverage relies on that shared check.
risks.evidence: selftest_security: missing setting, models:true, a truthy non-boolean, the UI client and the configuration default; the new checks fail against router 0.18.2 (missing setting denies concrete names).

risks.title: Cloud classification
risks.scenario: Incorrect declaration or classifier false negative forwards sensitive data.
risks.controls: Client class floor, cloud opt-out, secret scan. The cloud checks run on the final payload after memory insertion; the credential scan, the privacy rules and the classifier read inserted facts as text (router 0.21.1).
risks.next_action: Measure classifier quality on realistic personal and neutral texts; include tool results in the final-payload test.
risks.validation_gap: V5: final payload with memory is tested; end-to-end no-egress, classifier quality and tool results are not proven.

risks.title: Cloud transport/destinations
risks.scenario: HTTP provider or redirect leaves approved transport/host.
risks.controls: Allowlisted final HTTPS URL, with HTTP limited to explicit loopback. Every provider POST refuses redirects.
risks.next_action: Keep transport tests in CI and verify effective provider configuration when deploying.
risks.validation_gap: Synthetic endpoints cover application dispatch. Operator TLS termination and infrastructure remain deployment-specific.
risks.evidence: Both provider adapters reject 3xx before parsing or streaming the response; the second origin receives zero HTTP requests.

risks.title: Agent enrollment and compromise
risks.scenario: Pending-slot flood or compromised approved agent.
risks.controls: Ed25519 approval, bounded pending and per-IP admission. A wire-level test over the real tunnel endpoint shows that revocation ends waiting and streaming requests with the reason 'revoked', tells the agent, closes the connection and removes the node; the revoked key is refused on reconnect; new keys beyond the per-address limit are refused with 1008 and not registered, while an approved key still connects. The README asks to compare the UI fingerprint with skirnir-agent identity before approval (ADR-0066).
risks.next_action: Plausibility checks on reports of an approved agent; limit enrollment to known networks.
risks.validation_gap: V7: enrollment flood and revocation of active streams are tested at the wire; fingerprint verification is an operator step and a compromised approved agent can still report false load or answers.

risks.title: Resource and cost exhaustion
risks.scenario: Pre-auth flood, long streams or parallel costly inference.
risks.controls: Client rate and enrollment limits. Unauthenticated statistics capped at 1024 sources (LRU, evictions counted); their audit lines limited per source and event kind and by a global per-minute budget with withheld counts (ADR-0057). Since router 0.22.0 (ADR-0063) every configured client has max_concurrent requests in progress (default 4, 429 with Retry-After) and max_body_mib declared body size (default 16, 413), with per-client peak gauges.
risks.next_action: Measure peaks per client and tune limits; per-client cost bounds for cloud; bound chunked bodies per client; hostile-load test.
risks.validation_gap: V12: pre-auth state, audit volume and per-client concurrency and declared size are bounded and unit-tested; chunked bodies, per-client cost and hostile-load budgets remain.

risks.title: Session and memory isolation
risks.scenario: Stolen token or foreign UUID/project alias access.
risks.controls: Credential principals and scoped authorization. Route-inventory tests enumerate every registered session and memory route: none is reachable without an identity, and every owner-scoped session-store call uses the authenticated caller, never an owner taken from the request. With the gateway enabled every gateway route refuses requests without identity and the same alias maps to a bank per client; a token rotation refuses the old token on memory, gateway and session routes; a grant revoked by reload refuses recall.
risks.next_action: Deployment checks: separate tokens per client, minimal grants, and rotation after suspected exposure.
risks.validation_gap: V8: route, gateway, rotation and revocation behaviour is tested in process; deployment coverage remains.

risks.title: Memory poisoning and tool injection
risks.scenario: Shared writer injects false facts or tool instructions.
risks.controls: Grants, provenance and untrusted-context markers. Since router 0.20.0 a shared scope names its writers (memory_scopes.<scope>.writers, checked at load and per request, ADR-0060) and automatic recall skips requests that carry tools (skipped:tools) unless the project grant sets recall_into_tools: true (ADR-0059); opting in accepts the risk for that client.
risks.next_action: Review the writer list of every shared scope and every recall_into_tools opt-in; confirm or limit tool calls in clients that opt in; consider fact review before shared facts are recalled.
risks.validation_gap: V9: a listed writer can still plant false facts, and downstream agent/tool behavior of an opted-in client is outside unit-test coverage.

risks.title: Backend bypass and independent egress
risks.scenario: Direct backend access or its own cloud extraction.
risks.controls: Gateway-scoped grants on the router path only. The posture report flags static nodes over plain HTTP and a session store without verified TLS (ADR-0064); the agent example binds a child Ollama to loopback. `agent/Set-OllamaLoopback.cmd` binds node Ollama on Windows to loopback (agent child or desktop app), verifies the listeners and disables firewall rules that only opened Ollama (ADR-0072).
risks.next_action: Run Set-OllamaLoopback on every Windows node; inspect listening addresses and egress of Hindsight and PostgreSQL; separate service credentials.
risks.validation_gap: V5/V8: router-side transport is reported; backend listening addresses and egress need host inspection.

risks.title: Deletion retry and restoration
risks.scenario: Old outbox/backup resurrects data; session deletion leaves memory.
risks.controls: Outbox reauthorization, tombstones and selective deletion. Deletion journal outside the database re-applied at start before the outbox sends; admin reconcile for a restored Hindsight; optional deletion of a session's retained memory; deletion requested in flight takes over; stuck-deletion gauge; bounded decision capture (ADR-0076).
risks.next_action: Operator: keep deletions.jsonl out of database restores; decide delete_memory_with_session and retention days; verify derived Hindsight observations disappear with their document (live test).
risks.validation_gap: V11: restore and backup policies require integration/operational tests.

risks.title: Update trust and rollback
risks.scenario: Compromised release or old valid manifest.
risks.controls: Signed agent manifest and hash; separate Ollama source/checksum. Since agent 0.28.0 the agent refuses a signed version older than the running release (ADR-0054); deliberate rollback only with the node-local update.allow_downgrade switch. Since agent 0.29.0 several node-local keys can be trusted (update.public_keys) and deploy.py prepares and switches the signing key (ADR-0058). A rotation has been practised once in the deployment: agent 0.29.1 was signed only with the new key and accepted by every node before the old key was removed. Since ADR-0066 deploy.py --agent never creates a signing key; --create-agent-key makes the first one and --replace-lost-agent-key "<reason>" a recorded replacement; agent/Set-UpdateKey.ps1 performs the node step (Add, Complete, Replace) with backup, check-config and rollback.
risks.next_action: Keep the signing key offline from the router; consider a pre-trusted offline backup key in update.public_keys; keep the Ollama source check independent.
risks.validation_gap: V13: rotation practised once; lost-key recovery is tooled and unit-tested but not yet practised in the deployment.

risks.title: Host privilege escalation impact
risks.scenario: Router/agent compromise reaches privileged host operations.
risks.controls: Router systemd capabilities/filesystem restrictions. The agent forwards only inference, listing and version paths to the upstream and refuses Ollama downgrades without ollama_update.allow_downgrade; the root secret renderers source their access file only from a root-only folder the router cannot see or write, and the router unit sees its certificate folders read-only (certs, ADR-0073; tls of installations older than router.py --init, ADR-0082). render-env.sh refuses secret values with a line break and renders further names only when they end in _KEY or _TOKEN (ADR-0080). The Linux agent unit writes no program folder on PATH (binary in /opt/skirnir-agent) and keeps only CAP_SYS_ADMIN behind a system call filter without mount calls (ADR-0084); the agent refuses to start a child whose program, folder or a folder above someone besides the system and the administrators could change, unless user_writable_reason accepts it (ADR-0085); agent\Move-OllamaProtected.cmd moves a per-user Ollama.
risks.next_action: Dedicated router user and fuller unit directive set; separate privileged Windows agent operations.
risks.validation_gap: V13: unprivileged deployment and recovery still need staging.

risks.title: Logs telemetry and backups
risks.scenario: Metadata/secrets leak or local audit is altered.
risks.controls: Audit omits prompts and tokens; router-written files are owner-only (common.open_private, unit UMask=0077, ADR-0056); a CI canary test covers client and control authentication, inference paths and token rotation. Since router 0.21.1 the canaries also cover memory recall and retention, memory and inference backend errors and the session API, and an unexpected exception is logged by type and code location only (ADR-0062).
risks.next_action: Log rotation and retention, backup controls for these files, independent audit retention.
risks.validation_gap: V14: canaries cover authentication, inference, memory, session and backend error paths; rotation and backups are not covered.

risks.title: Supply chain and CI
risks.controls: pip-audit on runtime and optional requirement sets and govulncheck on every push, pull request and weekly, enforced by test/selftest_dependency_audit.py (ADR-0081); Dependabot (actions, Go, monitoring compose, decision-service Dockerfiles). Third-party actions pinned to commit SHAs, tools to versions, images and base images to digests, enforced by test/check_pinned_references.py (ADR-0055). Default-branch PR verification on an isolated hosted runner, App-bound merge status and same-dependency bump checks. Router hosts install pip packages only from router/requirements-lock.txt with --require-hashes --no-deps on top of distribution packages; CI installs requirements-ci-lock.txt; both locks are audited and compared with PyPI (ADR-0074). Release provenance: the agent is rebuilt from the tag and attested with SBOMs only if byte-identical (ADR-0075).
risks.next_action: Refresh the Python locks regularly (no Dependabot support for them); consider signing the router source archive; extend the rebuild to releases whose agent came from an earlier commit.
risks.validation_gap: V14: lock freshness depends on a manual refresh; distribution packages follow the distribution's updates; provenance covers the agent binaries, the router is released as source.
